newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa scores fresh seven-month low.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa scores fresh seven-month low.

text.p: London cocoa futures carved new seven-month lows on Friday under the weight of trade and speculative selling but prices stopped short of testing crucial support.
Selling pressure spilling over from Thursday's technically-disappointing close pushed the second-month benchmark to a session low of 963 stg in choppy trade.
"The fall was inevitable after the weak close yesterday," said one trader. "Everybody was disappointed that New York couldn't go above the $1,400 so people knocked the market down."
"There was a bear raid today," he added.
But traders cited fresh buying at the bottom, preventing March from sliding to 955, the low in March. They said 960 appeared to be a "buy" for the time being.
March ended just off the low at 964 stg a tonne, down eight on the day, while front December lost seven to end at 936.
Sterling's renewed strength also added to pressure, bringing back origin sellers, but the volume was small, traders said.
Turnover reached 5,337 lots which was considered average.
German trader Albrecht & Dill Gmbh said on Friday chocolate manufacturers were beginning to make an appearance in the market in response to price falls in futures.
Eyes are on the Ivory Coast which has announced its new season open, paving the way for new cocoa to hit export markets. Arrival figures are expected to creep in from next week.
Technical analysts said March would need to clear 990 stg for the outlook to improve, with 1,025 stg seen as a key barrier for upside attempts in the longer term.
